- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price is trending up.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 periods.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% over 3–5 days), check sentiment for bullish bias — if present, reduce forecast by 2–5% per day until sentiment shifts.
- If model consistently underestimates in high-sentiment environments, consider adding a 1–3% upward bias to forecast for next 2–3 periods.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >15% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment flips from bullish to bearish within 3 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 5 days if sentiment drops below 0.3.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid overfitting to recent 18-day history — if model is overfitting to recent highs, apply a 3–5 day lag correction (shift forecast down by 1–2% per day).
